chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Subbah, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who makes it incumbent upon himself for the sake of God to fast a specific day. He said: He always fasts, both in residence and during travel. The meaning in this report is that if he stipulated upon himself during the vow that he would fast during travel and residence, then that is binding upon him. And if he spoke generally without stipulating, then it is lifted from him during travel, according to what we have previously mentioned, and that which indicates this distinction.

key_terms.أَطْلَقَ: Spoke generally / did not specify conditions
key_terms.نَذْر: Vow, a pledge to perform an act of worship for the sake of God

ai.seo_question: Does a vow to fast a specific day remain obligatory while traveling if not explicitly specified?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between a specific vow (*nadhr muqayyad*) and a general vow (*nadhr mutlaq*) regarding fasting during travel. He clarifies that an explicit stipulation to fast in both states binds the individual regardless of location, whereas a general vow is subject to the standard juristic concession (*rukhsa*) for travelers, reflecting the nuanced application of conditional vows in Shia fiqh.
